blocks.text: Read the chapter with this setting in view: In Proverbs 8:22-31, personified Wisdom speaks of her relation to YHWH's ordering of the world and her delight before him and in humanity. It gives a starting point for following the chapter's own movement. The chapter itself should determine how far the point is taken. Interpretations differ on some details.

A literary feature to notice is that Proverbs 1-9 personifies Wisdom and Folly as women whose public calls, houses, meals, and paths embody rival forms of desire and lead respectively toward life and death. This form helps organize the chapter's claims. Notice it before drawing broader conclusions from a single phrase or image. The evidence leaves some details unresolved.
